posts.title: The water isn't coming back.
posts.caption: The water isn't coming back. A new study in Water Resources Research tracked 65 specialty crops county by county. Half the groundwater growing America's fruits, nuts, and vegetables is pumped faster than aquifers refill. In the Central Valley, more than 9 in 10 drops of specialty-crop irrigation come from that same overdraft. Almonds took more than 1 in 4 of those drops. The Valley feeds the country on water it can't replace. Full breakdown in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio. - Water Resources Research

posts.title: Newsom announces $1.3B for cleaner transit; Merced County to expand zero-emission microtransit
posts.caption:
Merced County is getting cleaner rides.

Governor Newsom announced nearly $1.3 billion for cleaner transit across California, and Merced County is expanding zero-emission microtransit. Smaller clean vehicles, reaching the neighborhoods big buses don't.

The funding also modernizes transit facilities and puts battery-electric buses on the road in Kings County. Cleaner air, better connections, and the Valley is part of it.

Full breakdown in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio. - Governor's Office

posts.title: New ICE detention facility opens in Appleton, Minnesota: 1,600 beds, $495.6 million
posts.caption:
Half a billion. 1,600 beds.

A new ICE detention facility opened this week in Appleton, Minnesota. DHS says it opened November 9. The site is the former Prairie Correctional Facility, a private prison empty since 2010, bought for $495.6 million. Full operation is expected by mid-2027.

It sits in the Eighth Circuit, where a federal appeals court has already approved holding many immigrants without bond.

Full record in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio.

- Source: MPR News / Fox 9

posts.title: LAUSD locks in $100M a year for Black Student Achievement Plan
posts.caption:
100M a year. Locked in.

LAUSD just voted to fund its Black Student Achievement Plan at $100M a year for the next two school years, above the $75M first proposed, while projecting a $3.6B shortfall the year after next. A federal probe into the program is still open.

When a board wants to fund something, the money appears. Follow the line items, not the press release. Read the full record in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio.

posts.title: Valedictorian detained at ICE check-in with her mother, held in Louisiana
posts.caption: She showed up. They took her. Maria Flores Garcia, valedictorian of Parkdale High School, walked into a routine ICE check-in with her mother. Both were detained. DHS says she has a 2021 removal order. She was first detained as a child in 2016, then released, then graduated first in her class. A check-in is supposed to be routine. When showing up gets you detained, the check-in is the trap. Follow @209media.connect. Full record in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio. - Source: FOX 5 DC

posts.title: Monterey County to ICE: Get Off Our Land. In Writing.
posts.caption: A county government just enforced its own vote, in writing. Monterey County sent ICE a cease-and-desist letter on November 5, ordering the agency off county-owned property used to stage immigration enforcement. The letter names four sites around Salinas, including Natividad Medical Center and the county jail. This is what enforcement of a September board vote looks like, and it is the test every California county is watching: what happens when a letter is not enough. Full breakdown in the 209connect newsletter every Tuesday, link in bio. - The Californian, Nov 5

posts.title: Randy Villegas defeats Valadao in CA-22
posts.caption: Randy Villegas, an educator and the son of Mexican immigrants, defeated David Valadao in California's 22nd district by running on the cost of living, health care cuts, and the immigration raids sweeping the Valley. Valadao told voters ICE only targets criminals, while reporting showed officers were told to arrest anybody. That gap is what voters answered. What does a new generation do with the job now? posts.title: The $75 Billion Trade: Jeffries Draws the Line on ICE Funding
posts.caption: Jeffries is offering a trade, not just a no. House Democrats will not fund what he calls a violent mass deportation machine, and $75 billion is already set aside for ICE through 2029. The systems question is what that money buys versus what a deal buys: bipartisan action this year on the Dream and Promise Act, a path to permanent residence for people who came here as kids and for people who lost protected status. The deadline is January, when the new Congress takes over. Funding fight or deal? That is the choice coming. Source: USA Today, Nov 9, 2026. Follow 209connect for the record behind the headline.

posts.title: Razor-thin 50.96% to 49.04% split. Boyenga took Atwater, McSwain in early mail. # #mercedcounty #usa
posts.caption:
715 votes. That is the entire spread separating Ana Boyenga (19,012) and Richard Lopez (18,297) with 37,309 votes logged so far.  

The green and blue map looks dramatic, but here is what the establishment isn't telling you: this board is still running off Batch 1.  

Batch 1 consists primarily of early vote-by-mail ballots returned weeks ago, which historically lean older and more conservative.  

What hasn’t hit the board yet?
Thousands of ballots dropped into county drop boxes on Tuesday.  

Postmarked mail arriving throughout the week.

Provisional and same-day registration ballots (currently sitting at zero).  

In Merced County, that late count heavily represents working families and the Latino vote.  

Boyenga took Atwater, McSwain, and Buhach on early mail, but the race is sitting on a razor-thin 50.96% to 49.04% split.  

Do not call this race early. The canvass has only just started.

Drop your thoughts below: Did you vote early, or did you hit the drop box on Tuesday? 🗳️

#MercedCounty #AtwaterCA #209Connect #CentralValley #MercedVotes
